back: Weight of localised raw materials ÷ weight of finished product. Above 1: near the raw material. Below 1: near the market.
Transport costs first, then labour costs and agglomeration, to find the least-cost location.
Isotim: line of equal total transport cost. Isodapane: line of equal extra transport cost; the critical isodapane equals the labour saving.
Average cost = fixed cost ÷ output + variable cost per unit; it falls as output rises (economies of scale).
Average cost rises when a firm is too large because of poor management, congestion and scarce inputs.
Backward: links to suppliers. Forward: links to users of the product.
Clustering of firms so that they share services, workers, suppliers and information.
High rents and congestion, lack of space, new markets, cheaper or more reliable power, incentives, poor infrastructure and loss of suppliers or customers.
Policy, special economic zones, power and water, rail routes, history and market size shape location as well as transport cost.
